messages:
customer_jane_acme: Hey team — we're seeing malformed JSON coming from the streamed /v1/generate endpoint. Our parser fails ~10% of the time, always on stream. Non-streaming responses are fine. Sample below.

ash_support: Sorry you're hitting this, Jane — can you paste the exact curl you used and one raw chunked response (not pretty-printed)? Also which model and region?

customer_jane_acme: Sure. Model: redwood/longform-1, region: us-west. Repro curl:
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?stream=true \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/longform-1","input":"summarize...","max_tokens":800}'
```
Raw response fragments (exact bytes):
```
data: {"id":"abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"{\"items\":[{\"id\":1,\"text\":\"hello\"},"},"index":0}]}
\n
data: {"id":"abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"{\"items\":[{\"id\":1,\"text\":\"hello\"},{\"id\":2,\"text\":\"worl"},"},"index":0}]}
\n
data: {"id":"abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"d\"}]} ,"index":0]}
```

We end up with fragments that break JSON boundaries (the first two chunks end with a comma then no closing bracket). Our client just concatenates content and then tries to JSON.parse — fails. When we re-request without stream=true, full JSON is valid.

ash_support: Thanks — that pattern (seems like chunks are splitting inside strings/arrays) looks like chunk-boundary truncation during streaming. A few quick checks: are you using any intermediate proxy/ingress that might buffer or cut connections? Any timeouts on your HTTP client? Also please send the request-id from response headers if you have it.

customer_jane_acme: No proxy, direct from our backend. Using node-fetch with default timeouts. We don't see any request-id header in the entries above (we can enable verbose logging).

ash_support: Can you reproduce with curl from your network? Your earlier curl was good — when run here I can see similar chunk splits. Two likely causes: 1) The server is streaming token-level deltas (intentionally fragmentary), and your client needs to reassemble; or 2) the connection is being reset mid-message (e.g., socket closes) and a final chunk with closing characters is missing.

nik_eng_runtime: looping in eng-runtime. Hey — can you attach the full raw TCP capture or paste the response headers for one of those requests? Also which client version of node-fetch? We had a regression previously where node's default http2/nghttp2 libs coalesced SSE frames differently.

customer_jane_acme: node-fetch 2.6.7. I ran curl -v, headers show:
```
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
< Connection: keep-alive
< x-request-id: req_7f9a1b2c
```
Raw body (we captured exact bytes) attached: first bytes end with "...,\n{\"id\":2,\"text\":\"worl"\n" then socket closed by peer.

nik_eng_runtime: Thanks, x-request-id present. I checked logs for req_7f9a1b2c — runtime shows the streaming generator emitted tokens up to the final token and signaled completion, but the runtime's HTTP flush to the TCP socket had a downstream write error: 
```
EPIPE while writing chunked frame to connection from worker-12
```
That means the client closed the connection before we could send the final bytes. So the server thinks it completed but client disconnected early, leading to truncated JSON on your side.

ash_support: Two paths: (A) Workaround: let the client attempt to reconnect and fetch the final payload non-streaming, or buffer chunks and accept partial JSON until you detect the 'done' event. If using our SDK, set stream_retry.enabled = true (SDK will fetch remaining data on reconnect). If using raw HTTP, do a fallback: re-request with stream=false when you detect an unexpected EOF.

customer_jane_acme: Is there a way to make the stream always send complete JSON fragments (NDJSON or explicit chunk delimiting) so clients that concatenate don't break?

nik_eng_runtime: We're considering a couple of improvements: 1) emit an explicit SSE event 'done' with a small JSON summary that is always flushed as a separate chunk — that gives a clear border; 2) support a 'json_mode=ndjson' param so the server emits one complete JSON object per event. For now, the supported pattern is clients should treat streaming as incremental tokens/deltas, not guaranteed chunk-aligned JSON.

ash_support: Practical immediate fix: update your node-fetch usage to increase socket keepalive and retry on ECONNRESET/EPIPE for streaming endpoints. Example patch: enable agent.keepAlive = true and set high socket timeout. Also, when you detect a truncated JSON parse error, call the non-streaming endpoint with same inputs and compare.

customer_jane_acme: Ok will try keepAlive + retry. One more ask — can eng-runtime add a server-side guard so when worker has completed but socket write fails, we write a short audit log indicating reason (client disconnect) and mark the request as "incomplete-stream"? That would make debugging easier.

nik_eng_runtime: Agree, filing a small internal ticket to add a clearer log line and emit an async post-event to the trace with status=INCOMPLETE_STREAM when write fails. I'll follow up here when deployed.

ash_support: Thanks everyone. Jane — can you confirm after you test (keepAlive + fallback) and paste the new x-request-id if you still see truncation? We'll escalate to SRE if needed. :thumbsup:

customer_jane_acme: Will do, thanks! :pray:
